color.background.code.added.highlight: Use for highlighted added code lines.
color.background.code.default: Use for the default background of code blocks and code diffs.
color.background.code.gutter: Use for the background of code gutters.
color.background.code.highlight: Use for highlighted unchanged code lines.
color.background.code.removed.highlight: Use for highlighted removed code lines.
color.background.disabled: Use for backgrounds of elements in a disabled state.
color.background.draghandle: Use for a prominent filled drag-handle background, such as a table grip. This is not a universal drag-handle icon or draggable-item background. Use color.icon.inverse for the handle icon. Keep selection and keyboard focus separate, and verify contrast on the actual surfaces in each theme.
color.background.droptarget: Use for the background of available drop destinations when the experience highlights eligible targets during a drag operation. Use color.background.droptarget.hovered for the current receiving destination. Ordinary pointer hover does not activate this state. Keep persistent selection, keyboard focus, and reserved placeholder space separate; preserve maintained insertion, combine, and nested-group treatments.
color.background.droptarget.hovered: Use for the background of the current drop destination during a drag operation. Apply while the dragged item is over the target. Ordinary pointer hover does not activate this state. For keyboard dragging, apply equivalent feedback to the current destination and keep keyboard focus identifiable independently. Do not apply to ineligible destinations.
color.background.input: Use for background of form UI elements, such as text fields, checkboxes, and radio buttons.
color.background.inverse.subtle: Use for backgrounds of elements on a bold background, such as in the buttons on spotlight cards.
color.background.inverse.subtle.hovered: Use for the hovered state of color.background.inverse.subtle
color.background.inverse.subtle.pressed: Use for the pressed state of color.background.inverse.subtle
color.background.neutral: The default background for neutral elements, such as default buttons.
color.background.neutral.subtle: Use for the background of elements that appear to have no background in a resting state, such as subtle buttons and menu items.
color.background.neutral.bold: A vibrant background option for neutral UI elements, such as announcement banners.
color.background.selected: Use for the background of an element that communicates selection, such as a selected navigation item, or the opened state of a dropdown trigger. Use color.background.selected.hovered or color.background.selected.pressed when interacting with a selected element. Selection is distinct from keyboard focus and hover alone.
color.background.selected.hovered: Use for the background of an element that is selected and hovered. This preserves selection while showing pointer hover; do not use for an unselected element or keyboard focus alone.
color.background.selected.pressed: Use for the background of an element that is selected and being pressed. Return to color.background.selected or color.background.selected.hovered when the press ends and the element remains selected. Do not use for an unselected element or keyboard focus alone.
color.background.selected.bold: Use for the bold background of selected controls, such as checked checkboxes and selected radio buttons. Pair with color.text.inverse or color.icon.inverse for foreground content. Do not use for primary actions or keyboard focus alone.
color.background.selected.bold.hovered: Use for the background of a selected control that uses color.background.selected.bold while it is hovered, such as a checked checkbox. Pair with color.text.inverse or color.icon.inverse for foreground content. Do not use for an unselected control or keyboard focus alone.
color.background.selected.bold.pressed: Use for the background of a selected control that uses color.background.selected.bold while it is being pressed, such as a checked checkbox. Pair with color.text.inverse or color.icon.inverse for foreground content. Do not use for an unselected control or keyboard focus alone.
color.background.brand.subtlest: Use for the background of elements used to reinforce our brand, but with less emphasis.
color.background.brand.bold: Use for the background of elements used to reinforce our brand, but with more emphasis.
color.background.brand.boldest: Use for the background of elements used to reinforce our brand, that need to stand out a lot.
color.background.danger: Use for backgrounds communicating critical information, such in error section messages.
color.background.danger.subtler: Use for backgrounds of danger lozenges and badges to ensure accessibility and desired visual appearance.
color.background.danger.subtle: Background colour for non-interactive elements communicating critical danger information (e.g. semantic badges, status pills, callout chips). Sits between subtler and bold in visual emphasis. Not for interactive surfaces — see color.background.danger.bold or color.background.danger.subtler for interactive states.
color.background.danger.bold: A vibrant background option for communicating critical information, such as in danger buttons and error banners.
color.background.warning: Use for backgrounds communicating caution, such as in warning section messages.
color.background.warning.subtler: Use for backgrounds of warning lozenges and badges to ensure accessibility and desired visual appearance.
color.background.warning.subtle: Background colour for non-interactive elements communicating caution (e.g. status pills, callout chips). Sits between subtler and bold in visual emphasis. Not for interactive surfaces — see color.background.warning.bold or color.background.warning.subtler for interactive states.
color.background.warning.bold: A vibrant background option for communicating caution, such as in warning buttons and warning banners.
color.background.success: Use for backgrounds communicating a favorable outcome, such as in success section messages.
color.background.success.subtler: Use for backgrounds of success lozenges and badges to ensure accessibility and desired visual appearance.
color.background.success.subtle: Background colour for non-interactive elements communicating success (e.g. semantic badges, status pills, callout chips). Sits between subtler and bold in visual emphasis. Not for interactive surfaces — see color.background.success.bold or color.background.success.subtler for interactive states.
color.background.success.bold: A vibrant background option for communicating a favorable outcome, such as in checked toggles.
color.background.discovery: Use for backgrounds communicating change or something new, such as in discovery section messages.
color.background.discovery.subtler: Use for backgrounds of discovery lozenges and badges to ensure accessibility and desired visual appearance.
color.background.discovery.subtle: Background colour for non-interactive elements communicating discovery (e.g. semantic badges, status pills, callout chips). Sits between subtler and bold in visual emphasis. Not for interactive surfaces — see color.background.discovery.bold or color.background.discovery.subtler for interactive states.
color.background.discovery.bold: A vibrant background option communicating change or something new, such as in onboarding spotlights.
color.background.information: Use for backgrounds communicating information or something in-progress, such as in information section messages.
color.background.information.subtler: Use for backgrounds of information lozenges and badges to ensure accessibility and desired visual appearance.
color.background.information.subtle: Background colour for non-interactive elements communicating information (e.g. semantic badges, status pills, callout chips). Sits between subtler and bold in visual emphasis. Not for interactive surfaces — see color.background.information.bold or color.background.information.subtler for interactive states.
color.background.information.bold: A vibrant background option for communicating information or something in-progress.
